header.name: MTO
header.authors_and_contributors: Oktay Boztas, Meire Ribeiro Domingos, Daniel Flórez-Orrego, EPFL IPESE research group
header.description: Light olefins (mainly ethylene and propylene) are produced from methanol, the products are separated by cryogenic distillation, and an olefin cracker improves the light olefin yield.
header.references:
[1] Hannula, I., Arpiainen, V., Light olefins and transport fuels from biomass residues via synthetic methanol: performance and cost analysis. Biomass Conversion and Biorefinery 5 (2015) 63-74, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s13399-014-0123-9;
[2] Boztas, O., Ribeiro-Domingos, M., Flórez-Orrego, D., Maréchal, F., Techno-economic and environmental assessment of sustainable thermochemical pathways for olefins production promoting carbon circularity. Renewable Energy (2025) 124303, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2025.124303

units.unit_description: This unit represents the conversion of 10000 kg/h of methanol into polymer grade ethylene and propylene and butene: MTO reactor with catalyst regeneration, quench, compression, cryogenic separation and olefin cracker. The non-valuable streams are burned with pure O2.
units.connectors_description: The unit takes methanol, oxygen and electricity, and delivers ethylene, propylene, butene, CO2 and waste water.

connectors.name: OXYGEN
connectors.description: Oxygen for the regenerator and the combustor

connectors.name: ETHYLENE
connectors.description: Polymer grade ethylene, pumped to 80 bar for pipeline export

connectors.name: CO2
connectors.description: CO2 from the regenerator, the combustor and the washing, after condensing the water

connectors.name: WASTEWATER
connectors.description: Process waste water, flash water and flue gas condensate
